newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply down, hit contract lows.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply down, hit contract lows.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed sharply weaker, having hit life-of-contract lows across the board early and continuing to rack up losses throughout the day.
The May contract settled down 3.10 at 76.35 cents per lb, having ranged from 78.00 to 76.00 cents, a new contract low. The back months ended 3.20 to 2.80 weaker.
Volume was estimated at 6,100 lots compared to Thursday's official 4,746 lots.
Traders blamed early losses on follow-through fund and speculative selling from Thursday's weak close, coupled with weak fundamentals.

The selling accelerated once May fell below support and its previous contract low of 77.50 cents. Trade buying and speculative short-covering held the market for most of the session but a late-session bout of selling just ahead of the close eroded support.
"The selling was technically-oriented but the movement figure and high imports didn't help," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
The Florida Citrus Processors Association put movement at 4.7 million gallons for the week ended March 22 compared with 6.1 million gallons the previous week.
Imports were 2.6 million gallons compared with 734,141 gallons the previous week.
Brazil said late last week that exports in the first seven months were higher than year-ago levels. U.S. demand, meanwhile, shows no sign of strengthening.
"In order for the market to stage a rebound from present low levels we would need to see a strong jump in retail demand," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said in a weekly letter.
"This has yet to occur and as a result, we would have to expect prices to remain soft," she said.
